Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Separate structural clues from exact cell placement: for expansions, compare dimensions, preserved regions, block histograms, then positions; matching histograms proves only a permutation. For sparse, interrupted outlines, check whether markers trace an enclosing frame before filling gaps; if so, fill only missing border cells. For diagonal stripe patterns, compare cells by `r+c` and `r-c` to identify the stripe direction, then read demonstrated outputs along that diagonal index to infer the cycle, phase, and any unequal run widths. A period that merely fits sparse clues does not determine unseen colors: request another demo rather than filling unknown residues by guess or nearest-neighbor. Implement or fix `transform(grid)` and run it against every exact pair received; require exact input-output matches before submitting. When transcribing grids for local testing, assert row count and every row width against the stated dimensions; fix transcription errors before trusting results.
3. Run the verified transform on the test input and copy its returned grid exactly into the required submit action; do not manually adjust cells. Keep the required action JSON as the final line.
4. After verdict, save the transform that reproduces all received pairs at `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing the old version, then finish only when the instance is over.

    # Combine the two 4-row masks separated by the solid 4 divider.
    divider = next(r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if row and all(v == 4 for v in row))
    top = grid[:divider]
    bottom = grid[divider + 1:]
    return [[3 if top[r][c] != 0 or bottom[r][c] != 0 else 0
             for c in range(len(top[r]))] for r in range(len(top))]
"
